units.zh: 老子曰：「至治之極，鄰國相望，雞狗之聲相聞，民各甘其食，美其服，安其俗，樂其業，至老死，不相往來。」
units.en: Laozi said: 'In the most perfectly governed age, neighboring states are within sight of one another, the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs can be heard across the border, the people savor their own food, take pride in their own clothing, rest content in their own customs, and delight in their own occupations — and they grow old and die without ever setting foot in one another's lands.'
units.literal: Laozi said: 'At the height of perfect governance, neighboring states can see one another, the sounds of roosters and dogs can be heard between them, the people each relish their own food, admire their own clothes, feel at ease in their own customs, and take pleasure in their own work; they grow old and die without ever visiting one another.'

units.zh: 必用此為務，輓近世涂民耳目，則幾無行矣。
units.en: If one insists on making this the governing principle, attempting to drag the modern world backward by stopping up the eyes and ears of the people, the task would prove virtually impossible.
units.literal: If one insists on making this the guiding principle and tries to pull the modern world back by stopping up the people's eyes and ears, then it is virtually impossible to put into practice.

units.zh: 太史公曰：夫神農以前，吾不知已。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Of the ages before Shennong, I have no knowledge.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Of the ages before Shennong, I have no knowledge.

units.zh: 至若詩書所述虞夏以來，耳目欲極聲色之好，口欲窮芻豢之味，身安逸樂，而心誇矜輓能之榮使。
units.en: But as the Odes and the Documents attest, from the time of Yu and Xia onward, the ears and eyes of the people have craved the ultimate in music and beauty, their palates have sought the finest flavors of grain-fed and pasture-raised meats, their bodies have desired ease and comfort, and their hearts have swelled with pride at the glory that ability and influence can bring.
units.literal: But as the Odes and Documents describe from the times of Yu and Xia onward, people's ears and eyes have sought the utmost pleasure in music and beauty, their mouths have craved the finest flavors of grain-fed and pasture-fed meats, their bodies have desired ease and comfort, and their hearts have swelled with pride in the glory and influence that ability can bring.

units.zh: 俗之漸民久矣，雖戶說以眇論，終不能化。
units.en: These habits have seeped into the people over such a long span of time that even going door to door preaching subtle doctrines could never change them.
units.literal: These customs have permeated the people for a long time; even if one went door to door expounding subtle doctrines, one could never transform them.

units.zh: 故善者因之，其次利道之，其次教誨之，其次整齊之，最下者與之爭。
units.en: And so the wisest ruler works with the natural grain of things; the next best guides the people through the inducement of profit; the next best instructs and admonishes them; the next best imposes regulation and order upon them; and the very worst contends against them.
units.literal: Therefore, the best ruler works with the natural flow; the next best guides the people through profit; the next best instructs and admonishes them; the next best regulates and orders them; the worst competes against them.

units.zh: 夫山西饒材、竹、穀、纑、旄、玉石；
units.en: The region west of the mountains abounds in timber, bamboo, grain, hemp, yak tails, jade, and fine stone;
units.literal: Now, west of the mountains there is an abundance of timber, bamboo, grain, hemp, yak tails, and jade and stone;

units.zh: 山東多魚、鹽、漆、絲、聲色；
units.en: The region east of the mountains produces abundant fish, salt, lacquer, silk, and entertainments of music and beauty;
units.literal: east of the mountains there is much fish, salt, lacquer, silk, and music and beauty;

units.zh: 江南出枏、梓、薑、桂、金、錫、連、丹沙、犀、瑁、珠璣、齒革；
units.en: The lands south of the Yangtze yield nanmu and catalpa wood, ginger, cassia, gold, tin, lead, cinnabar, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, pearls, ivory, and hides;
units.literal: south of the Yangtze produces nanmu timber, catalpa wood, ginger, cassia, gold, tin, lead, cinnabar, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, pearls, ivory, and hides;

units.zh: 龍門、碣石北多馬、牛、羊、旃裘、筋角；
units.en: North of Longmen and Jieshi one finds horses, cattle, sheep, felt garments, sinews, and horns in abundance;
units.literal: north of Longmen and Jieshi there are many horses, cattle, sheep, felt garments, sinews, and horns;

units.zh: 銅、鐵則千里往往山出棋置：此其大較也。
units.en: And copper and iron are found scattered throughout the mountains across a thousand li, dotted about like pieces on a chessboard. These are the broad outlines.
units.literal: as for copper and iron, throughout a thousand li the mountains yield them, scattered about like pieces on a chessboard: these are the broad outlines.

units.zh: 皆中國人民所喜好謠俗被服飲食奉生送死之具也。
units.en: All these are the goods in which the people of the Central States take delight — the substance of their customs, their clothing, and food, their sustenance in life and their provisions for the dead.
units.literal: All of these are the goods that the people of the Central States delight in — the stuff of their customs and songs, their clothing and food, their sustenance in life and provisions for death.

units.zh: 故待農而食之，虞而出之，工而成之，商而通之。
units.en: And so these goods depend on farmers to produce them, foresters to extract them, artisans to fashion them, and merchants to circulate them.
units.literal: Therefore, they depend on farmers to produce food, foresters to extract raw materials, artisans to fashion goods, and merchants to circulate them.

units.zh: 此寧有政教發徵期會哉？
units.en: Was any of this ever brought about by government edicts, official levies, or appointed schedules?
units.literal: Was this ever a matter of government edicts, levies, or appointed schedules?

units.zh: 人各任其能，竭其力，以得所欲。
units.en: Each person simply employs his own abilities and exhausts his own strength to obtain what he desires.
units.literal: Each person employs his own ability and exhausts his own strength to obtain what he desires.

units.zh: 故物賤之徵貴，貴之徵賤，各勸其業，樂其事，若水之趨下，日夜無休時，不召而自來，不求而民出之。
units.en: When goods are cheap, it is a sign that prices will rise; when expensive, that they will fall. Each person is spurred on in his own trade and takes delight in his own work. Like water flowing downhill, day and night without ceasing, goods come without being summoned, and the people produce them without being asked.
units.literal: Therefore, when goods are cheap, that is a sign they will become expensive; when expensive, a sign they will become cheap. Each person is encouraged in his own trade and takes pleasure in his own work, like water flowing downward day and night without rest — without being summoned they come of their own accord, without being asked the people produce of themselves.

units.zh: 豈非道之所符，而自然之驗邪？
units.en: Is this not the very manifestation of the Way, and the proof of what arises naturally?
units.literal: Is this not the sign of the Way, and the proof of what is natural?

units.zh: 《周書》曰：「農不出則乏其食，工不出則乏其事，商不出則三寶絕，虞不出則財匱少。」
units.en: The Book of Zhou says: 'When farmers do not produce, food grows scarce. When artisans do not produce, goods grow scarce. When merchants do not trade, the three treasures are cut off. When foresters do not extract, resources are depleted.'
units.literal: The Book of Zhou says: 'When farmers do not produce, food is scarce; when artisans do not produce, goods are scarce; when merchants do not trade, the three treasures are cut off; when foresters do not extract, resources are depleted.'

units.zh: 財匱少而山澤不辟矣。
units.en: When resources are depleted, the mountains and marshlands are left unopened.
units.literal: When resources are depleted and scarce, the mountains and marshes are not opened up.

units.zh: 此四者，民所衣食之原也。
units.en: These four occupations are the wellspring from which the people draw their clothing and food.
units.literal: These four occupations are the source from which the people clothe and feed themselves.

units.zh: 原大則饒，原小則鮮。
units.en: When the source is ample, there is abundance; when it is narrow, there is scarcity.
units.literal: When the source is large there is abundance; when the source is small there is scarcity.

units.zh: 上則富國，下則富家。
units.en: At the top, it enriches the state; at the bottom, it enriches the household.
units.literal: Above, it enriches the state; below, it enriches the household.

units.zh: 貧富之道，莫之奪予，而巧者有餘，拙者不足。
units.en: The path to wealth and poverty is not imposed by anyone from above. The skillful end up with a surplus; the clumsy are left wanting.
units.literal: The way of poverty and wealth — no one seizes or bestows it; yet the skillful have surplus, and the clumsy fall short.

units.zh: 故太公望封於營丘，地澙鹵，人民寡，於是太公勸其女功，極技巧，通魚鹽，則人物歸之，繦至而輻湊。
units.en: When the Grand Duke Wang was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, the land was salty and barren and the people few. He encouraged women's handicrafts, perfected artisanal skills, and opened up trade in fish and salt. People and goods streamed toward him, arriving as if carried in swaddling clothes, converging like spokes toward the hub of a wheel.
units.literal: Therefore, when the Grand Duke Wang was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, the land was salty and alkaline and the people were few. Thereupon the Grand Duke encouraged women's handicrafts, perfected technical skills, and opened trade in fish and salt; then people and goods flowed to him, arriving in swaddling clothes and converging like the spokes of a wheel.

units.zh: 故齊冠帶衣履天下，海岱之閒斂袂而往朝焉。
units.en: And so Qi came to supply caps, sashes, clothing, and shoes to the entire realm. From the shores of the sea to the slopes of Mount Tai, the people gathered their sleeves and hastened to pay homage at Qi's court.
units.literal: Thus, Qi supplied caps, sashes, clothing, and shoes to all under Heaven, and between the sea and Mount Tai people gathered their sleeves and went to pay homage at its court.

units.zh: 其後齊中衰，管子修之，設輕重九府，則桓公以霸，九合諸侯，一匡天下；
units.en: Later, when Qi fell into decline, Guan Zhong revived it by establishing the system of price regulation and the Nine Treasuries. With this, Duke Huan achieved hegemony, convened the feudal lords nine times, and brought order to the entire realm;
units.literal: Later, when Qi fell into decline, Guan Zhong restored it by establishing the system of light-and-heavy regulations and the Nine Treasuries; thereupon Duke Huan achieved hegemony, convened the feudal lords nine times, and brought order to all under Heaven;

units.zh: 而管氏亦有三歸，位在陪臣，富於列國之君。
units.en: And Guan Zhong himself, though he held only the rank of a vassal's vassal, possessed the 'three returns' and amassed wealth exceeding that of the rulers of the feudal states.
units.literal: and Guan Zhong himself possessed the 'three returns,' held the rank of a mere vassal's vassal, yet was wealthier than the rulers of the feudal states.

units.zh: 是以齊富彊至於威、宣也。
units.en: And so the wealth and power of Qi endured all the way down to the reigns of Kings Wei and Xuan.
units.literal: Thus, the wealth and power of Qi continued down to the reigns of Kings Wei and Xuan.

units.zh: 故曰：「倉廩實而知禮節，衣食足而知榮辱。」
units.en: Thus, the saying goes: 'When the granaries are full, the people learn propriety and ritual; when clothing and food are sufficient, the people learn honor and shame.'
units.literal: Therefore, it is said: 'When the granaries are full, the people come to know propriety and ritual; when clothing and food are sufficient, the people come to know honor and shame.'

units.zh: 禮生於有而廢於無。
units.en: Ritual is born of plenty and withers in want.
units.literal: Ritual is born from abundance and perishes from want.

units.zh: 故君子富，好行其德；
units.en: When a gentleman grows wealthy, he takes delight in practicing virtue;
units.literal: Therefore, when a gentleman is wealthy, he delights in practicing virtue;

units.zh: 小人富，以適其力。
units.en: When a petty man grows wealthy, he channels it into the exercise of his strength.
units.literal: when a petty man is wealthy, he uses it to apply his strength.

units.zh: 淵深而魚生之，山深而獸往之，人富而仁義附焉。
units.en: Where the waters run deep, fish are born. Where the mountains are deep, beasts make their home. Where the people are wealthy, benevolence and righteousness attach themselves naturally.
units.literal: Where the abyss is deep, fish are born; where the mountains are deep, beasts go; where people are wealthy, benevolence and righteousness attach themselves.

units.zh: 富者得埶益彰，失埶則客無所之，以而不樂。
units.en: When the wealthy gain influence, their renown shines all the brighter. When they lose it, their guests have nowhere to turn, and discontent sets in.
units.literal: When the wealthy gain influence, their renown grows all the greater; when they lose influence, their guests have nowhere to go, and therefore they are unhappy.

units.zh: 夷狄益甚。
units.en: Among the barbarian peoples, this is even more pronounced.
units.literal: Among the barbarians this is all the more pronounced.

units.zh: 諺曰：「千金之子，不死於市。」
units.en: As the proverb puts it: 'The son of a family worth a thousand in gold will never die in the marketplace.'
units.literal: The proverb says: 'The son of a family worth a thousand in gold does not die in the marketplace.'

units.zh: 此非空言也。
units.en: This was no mere empty saying.
units.literal: This is no empty saying.

units.zh: 故曰：「天下熙熙，皆為利來；
units.en: Thus, it is said: 'All under heaven bustles and stirs — everyone comes for the sake of profit;
units.literal: Therefore, it is said: 'All under heaven bustles and stirs — all come for the sake of profit;

units.zh: 天下壤壤，皆為利往。」
units.en: All under heaven clamors and jostles — everyone goes for the sake of profit.'
units.literal: all under heaven clamors and jostles — all go for the sake of profit.'

units.zh: 夫千乘之王，萬家之侯，百室之君，尚猶患貧，而況匹夫編戶之民乎！
units.en: If kings of a thousand chariots, marquises of ten thousand households, and lords of a hundred estates still worry about poverty, how much more so the common man, a mere registered householder!
units.literal: Now, kings of a thousand chariots, marquises of ten thousand households, lords of a hundred estates — even they still worry about poverty. How much more so the common man, a mere registered householder!

units.zh: 昔者越王句踐困於會稽之上，乃用范蠡、計然。
units.en: In former times, King Goujian of Yue found himself besieged atop Mount Kuaiji. He turned to Fan Li and Ji Ran for counsel.
units.literal: In former times, King Goujian of Yue was trapped on Mount Kuaiji, and thereupon employed Fan Li and Ji Ran.

units.zh: 計然曰：「知斗則修備，時用則知物，二者形則萬貨之情可得而觀已。
units.en: Ji Ran said: 'Know that war is coming, and you prepare your defenses. Know what the season demands, and you understand the nature of goods. When both of these are perceived, the workings of all ten thousand commodities can be grasped.
units.literal: Ji Ran said: 'If one knows war is coming, one prepares for it; if one knows what the season demands, one understands goods. When both of these take shape, the nature of all ten thousand commodities can be grasped and observed.

units.zh: 故歲在金，穰；
units.en: When the year corresponds to Metal, there is abundance;
units.literal: Therefore, when the year corresponds to Metal, there is abundance;

units.zh: 水，毀；
units.en: When to Water, ruin;
units.literal: when to Water, there is ruin;

units.zh: 木，饑；
units.en: When to Wood, famine;
units.literal: when to Wood, there is famine;

units.zh: 火，旱。
units.en: And when to Fire, drought.
units.literal: when to Fire, there is drought.

units.zh: 旱則資舟，水則資車，物之理也。
units.en: In times of drought, invest in boats; in times of flood, invest in carts. Such is the principle governing commodities.
units.literal: In drought, invest in boats; in flood, invest in carts — this is the principle of commodities.

units.zh: 六歲穰，六歲旱，十二歲一大饑。
units.en: Every six years brings abundance, every six years drought, and once in twelve years a great famine.
units.literal: Six years of plenty, six years of drought, and once every twelve years a great famine.

units.zh: 夫糶，二十病農，九十病末。
units.en: As for grain prices: when they fall to twenty cash, the farmers suffer; when they rise to ninety, the merchants suffer.
units.literal: Now, regarding grain prices: at twenty cash, the farmer suffers; at ninety cash, the merchant suffers.

units.zh: 末病則財不出，農病則草不辟矣。
units.en: When the merchants suffer, wealth ceases to circulate. When the farmers suffer, the land is left uncultivated.
units.literal: When merchants suffer, wealth does not circulate; when farmers suffer, the land is not cleared.

units.zh: 上不過八十，下不減三十，則農末俱利，平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。
units.en: If the price never exceeds eighty nor falls below thirty, then both farmer and merchant profit together. Grain prices are stabilized, goods are balanced, and the markets and border passes never run short. This is the way to govern a state.
units.literal: If the price does not exceed eighty above and does not fall below thirty below, then both farmers and merchants profit, grain prices are equalized and goods are balanced, markets and border passes lack nothing — this is the way to govern a state.

units.zh: 積著之理，務完物，無息幣。
units.en: The principle of accumulation and storage: strive to keep goods in perfect condition, and never let money sit idle.
units.literal: The principle of accumulating and storing: strive to keep goods intact, and do not let money sit idle.

units.zh: 以物相貿易，腐敗而食之貨勿留，無敢居貴。
units.en: When trading goods, do not hold on to perishable commodities, and never dare to hoard in hopes of driving up the price.
units.literal: In bartering goods, do not hold on to perishable foodstuffs, and do not dare hoard in hopes of high prices.

units.zh: 論其有餘不足，則知貴賤。
units.en: Examine what is in surplus and what is in shortage, and you will know what is dear and what is cheap.
units.literal: By examining what is in surplus and what is in shortage, one can know what is dear and what is cheap.

units.zh: 貴上極則反賤，賤下極則反貴。
units.en: When prices rise to the extreme, they will reverse and fall. When they fall to the extreme, they will reverse and rise.
units.literal: When prices rise to their extreme, they will reverse and become cheap; when they fall to their extreme, they will reverse and become dear.

units.zh: 貴出如糞土，賤取如珠玉。
units.en: When prices are high, sell as though throwing away dirt. When prices are low, buy as though acquiring pearls and jade.
units.literal: Sell when prices are high as though casting away dirt and dung; buy when prices are low as though acquiring pearls and jade.

units.zh: 財幣欲其行如流水。」
units.en: Wealth and currency must flow like running water.'
units.literal: Wealth and currency should be kept flowing like running water.'

units.zh: 修之十年，國富，厚賂戰士，士赴矢石，如渴得飲，遂報彊吳，觀兵中國，稱號「五霸」。
units.en: Goujian followed these principles for ten years, and his state grew rich. He lavished rewards upon his warriors, and the soldiers charged into arrows and stones as eagerly as a thirsty man reaching for drink. He avenged himself upon mighty Wu, paraded his armies before the Central States, and earned the title "one of the Five Hegemons."
units.literal: He cultivated these principles for ten years, and the state grew rich. He lavished rewards on his warriors, and the soldiers rushed into arrows and stones as eagerly as a thirsty man reaching for drink. He avenged himself upon mighty Wu, paraded his armies before the Central States, and was numbered among the 'Five Hegemons.'

units.zh: 范蠡既雪會稽之恥，乃喟然而嘆曰：「計然之策七，越用其五而得意。
units.en: After Fan Li had washed away the humiliation of Kuaiji, he heaved a deep sigh and said: 'Of Ji Ran's seven strategies, Yue employed only five and achieved everything it sought.
units.literal: After Fan Li had wiped away the shame of Kuaiji, he sighed deeply and said: 'Of Ji Ran's seven strategies, Yue employed five and achieved its aims.

units.zh: 既已施於國，吾欲用之家。」
units.en: Now that they have been applied to the state, I intend to apply them to my own household.'
units.literal: Since these have already been applied to the state, I wish to apply them to my own household.'

units.zh: 乃乘扁舟浮於江湖，變名易姓，適齊為鴟夷子皮，之陶為朱公。
units.en: He boarded a small boat and set out across the rivers and lakes, changing his name and surname. In Qi he was known as Chiyi Zipi; when he moved to Tao, he took the name Tao Zhugong.
units.literal: He then boarded a small boat and floated upon the rivers and lakes, changed his name and surname, went to Qi where he became known as Chiyi Zipi, and moved to Tao where he became known as Tao Zhugong.

units.zh: 朱公以為陶天下之中，諸侯四通，貨物所交易也。
units.en: Zhugong judged Tao to be the center of the realm, with roads leading to the feudal lords in all four directions — a natural hub for the exchange of goods.
units.literal: Zhugong considered Tao to be the center of the realm, with routes to the feudal lords open in all four directions — a place where goods were traded.

units.zh: 乃治產積居。
units.en: He set about managing his estates and accumulating goods.
units.literal: He then managed his property and accumulated stores.

units.zh: 與時逐而不責於人。
units.en: He pursued the opportunities of the moment without making demands on others.
units.literal: He pursued opportunities as they arose and did not impose demands on others.

units.zh: 故善治生者，能擇人而任時。
units.en: Thus, the man who excels at managing his livelihood knows how to choose the right people and seize the right moment.
units.literal: Therefore, one skilled at managing livelihood can choose the right people and seize the right moment.

units.zh: 十九年之中三致千金，再分散與貧交疏昆弟。
units.en: Within nineteen years he amassed a fortune of a thousand in gold three times over, and twice gave it all away to poor friends and distant kinsmen.
units.literal: Within nineteen years he amassed a thousand in gold three times, and twice distributed it to poor friends and distant kinsmen.

units.zh: 此所謂富好行其德者也。
units.en: This is what it means to be wealthy and to delight in practicing virtue.
units.literal: This is what is called being wealthy and delighting in practicing virtue.

units.zh: 後年衰老而聽子孫，子孫修業而息之，遂至巨萬。
units.en: In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed the business to his sons and grandsons. They carried on and expanded it, eventually amassing an enormous fortune.
units.literal: In his later years, growing old, he entrusted affairs to his sons and grandsons; they carried on the business and grew it, eventually reaching enormous wealth.

units.zh: 故言富者皆稱陶朱公。
units.en: And so whenever people speak of great wealth, they invoke the name of Tao Zhugong.
units.literal: Therefore, when people speak of wealth, they all cite Tao Zhugong.

units.zh: 子贛既學於仲尼，退而仕於衛，廢著鬻財於曹、魯之閒，七十子之徒，賜最為饒益。
units.en: Zigong studied under Confucius, then withdrew to serve in Wei, trading goods and accumulating wealth between Cao and Lu. Of all the seventy disciples, Zigong was by far the most prosperous.
units.literal: Zigong, after studying under Confucius, withdrew and served in Wei, and traded goods and amassed wealth between Cao and Lu. Among the seventy disciples, Zigong was the most prosperous.

units.zh: 原憲不厭糟糠，匿於窮巷。
units.en: Yuan Xian could not even fill his belly with chaff and dregs, and lived hidden away in a destitute alley.
units.literal: Yuan Xian did not even have his fill of chaff and dregs, and hid in an impoverished alley.

units.zh: 子貢結駟連騎，束帛之幣以聘享諸侯，所至，國君無不分庭與之抗禮。
units.en: Zigong rode in a four-horse carriage with a retinue of mounted escorts, bearing bundles of silk as gifts to visit and feast the feudal lords. Wherever he went, rulers divided the court and received him with the courtesy due an equal.
units.literal: Zigong rode in a four-horse carriage followed by a retinue of riders, bearing bundles of silk as gifts to visit and feast the feudal lords; wherever he went, no ruler failed to divide the court with him and treat him as an equal.

units.zh: 夫使孔子名布揚於天下者，子貢先後之也。
units.en: It was Zigong, working tirelessly before and after, who caused the name of Confucius to be spread and celebrated throughout the realm.
units.literal: Now, the one who caused the name of Confucius to be spread and celebrated throughout the realm was Zigong, supporting him from first to last.

units.zh: 此所謂得埶而益彰者乎？
units.en: Is this not a case of gaining influence and thereby shining all the more brightly?
units.literal: Is this not what is called gaining influence and thereby growing all the more illustrious?

units.zh: 白圭，周人也。
units.en: Bai Gui was a man from the state of Zhou.
units.literal: Bai Gui was a man of Zhou.

units.zh: 當魏文侯時，李克務盡地力，而白圭樂觀時變，故人棄我取，人取我與。
units.en: In the time of Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke devoted himself to maximizing the yield of the land, while Bai Gui took delight in reading the shifts of the seasons. His principle was: what others discard, I collect; what others seek, I release.
units.literal: In the time of Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke devoted himself to exhausting the productive capacity of the land, while Bai Gui delighted in observing the changes of the seasons; therefore, what others discard, I take; what others take, I give.

units.zh: 夫歲孰取穀，予之絲漆；
units.en: In a good harvest year, buy grain and offer silk and lacquer in exchange;
units.literal: When the harvest year is good, buy grain and give silk and lacquer in exchange;

units.zh: 繭出取帛絮，予之食。
units.en: When the cocoons come in, buy silk floss and cloth, and offer food in exchange.
units.literal: when cocoons come out, buy silk floss and cloth, and give food in exchange.

units.zh: 太陰在卯，穰；
units.en: When Taiyin is in mao, crops will be abundant;
units.literal: When Jupiter is in the mao position, there is abundance;

units.zh: 明歲衰惡。
units.en: The following year will bring decline and hardship.
units.literal: the following year there will be decline and hardship.

units.zh: 至午，旱；
units.en: When Jupiter reaches the wu position, there is drought;
units.literal: When it reaches the wu position, drought;

units.zh: 明歲美。
units.en: The following year will be a good one.
units.literal: the following year will be good.

units.zh: 至酉，穰；
units.en: When it reaches the you position, there is abundance;
units.literal: When it reaches the you position, abundance;

units.zh: 明歲衰惡。
units.en: The following year will bring decline and hardship.
units.literal: the following year there will be decline and hardship.

units.zh: 至子，大旱；
units.en: When it reaches the zi position, there is severe drought;
units.literal: When it reaches the zi position, severe drought;

units.zh: 明歲美，有水。
units.en: The following year will be a good one, though with flooding.
units.literal: the following year will be good, with flooding.

units.zh: 至卯，積著率歲倍。
units.en: By the time it returns to the mao position, accumulated stores have generally doubled each year.
units.literal: When it returns to the mao position, accumulated stores generally double each year.

units.zh: 欲長錢，取下穀；
units.en: To increase your cash, buy low-grade grain;
units.literal: If you wish to increase your money, buy low-grade grain;

units.zh: 長石斗，取上種。
units.en: To increase your stores of grain by the bushel, buy top-grade seed.
units.literal: if you wish to increase your bushels and pecks, buy top-grade seed.

units.zh: 能薄飲食，忍嗜欲，節衣服，與用事僮仆同苦樂，趨時若猛獸摯鳥之發。
units.en: He ate sparingly, suppressed his desires, and economized on clothing. He shared both hardship and ease with his servants, and when opportunity arose, he seized it with the ferocity of a predatory beast or a raptor striking its prey.
units.literal: He could eat sparingly, suppress his desires, economize on clothing, share both hardships and pleasures with his working servants, and seize the moment as fiercely as a predatory beast or a striking bird of prey.

units.zh: 故曰：「吾治生產，猶伊尹、呂尚之謀，孫吳用兵，商鞅行法是也。
units.en: He declared: 'My approach to managing commerce and production is comparable to the stratagems of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, the military art of Sunzi and Wu Qi, and Shang Yang's implementation of the law.
units.literal: Therefore, he said: 'My management of livelihood and production is like the stratagems of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, the deployment of troops by Sun and Wu, and the implementation of law by Shang Yang.

units.zh: 是故其智不足與權變，勇不足以決斷，仁不能以取予，彊不能有所守，雖欲學吾術，終不告之矣。」
units.en: If a man's intelligence is insufficient for weighing circumstances and adapting, and if his courage is insufficient for decisive action, he may wish to learn my methods, but I will never teach him. If his benevolence is insufficient for knowing when to give and when to take, and if his firmness is insufficient for holding his ground, I will never teach him.'
units.literal: Therefore, if one's intelligence is insufficient for weighing circumstances and adapting, one's courage insufficient for making decisions, one's benevolence insufficient for knowing when to give and take, and one's firmness insufficient for holding one's ground — though one may wish to learn my methods, I will never divulge them.'

units.zh: 蓋天下言治生祖白圭。
units.en: And so throughout the realm, all who speak of managing commerce regard Bai Gui as their founder.
units.literal: Thus, all under heaven who speak of managing livelihood regard Bai Gui as their founder.

units.zh: 白圭其有所試矣，能試有所長，非茍而已也。
units.en: Bai Gui had truly put his principles to the test. His proven methods had real substance — they were no idle boast.
units.literal: Bai Gui had indeed put his principles to the test; his tested methods had genuine strengths — it was not mere idle talk.

units.zh: 猗頓用盬鹽起。
units.en: Yi Dun built his fortune through the salt trade of Anyi.
units.literal: Yi Dun rose through the trade of Anyi salt.

units.zh: 而邯鄲郭縱以鐵冶成業，與王者埒富。
units.en: Guo Zong of Handan built his enterprise through iron smelting, amassing wealth to rival that of kings.
units.literal: And Guo Zong of Handan established his enterprise through iron smelting, amassing wealth rivaling that of kings.

units.zh: 烏氏倮牧，及眾，斥賣，求奇繒物，閒獻遺戎王。
units.en: Luo of the Wushi clan began as a herdsman. When his flocks grew large, he sold them off, invested in rare silks and exotic goods, and periodically presented gifts to the Rong king.
units.literal: Luo of the Wushi clan herded livestock; when his herds grew numerous, he sold them off, sought rare silks and unusual goods, and from time to time presented gifts to the Rong king.

units.zh: 戎王什倍其償，與之畜，畜至用谷量馬牛。
units.en: The Rong king repaid him tenfold in livestock. His herds grew so vast that his horses and cattle were counted by the valley.
units.literal: The Rong king repaid him tenfold, giving him livestock; his livestock grew until his horses and cattle were measured by the valley.

units.zh: 秦始皇帝令倮比封君，以時與列臣朝請。
units.en: The First Emperor of Qin decreed that Luo be accorded the status of an enfeoffed lord, attending court audiences alongside the ranked ministers at the proper times.
units.literal: The First Emperor of Qin ordered that Luo be treated as the equal of an enfeoffed lord, and at the proper times he attended court audiences alongside the ranked ministers.

units.zh: 而巴[蜀]寡婦清，其先得丹穴，而擅其利數世，家亦不訾。
units.en: The Widow Qing of Ba descended from a family that had discovered cinnabar mines and monopolized their profits for generations. Her household's wealth was beyond reckoning.
units.literal: And the Widow Qing of Ba, whose ancestors had discovered cinnabar mines and monopolized their profits for several generations — her household's wealth was incalculable.

units.zh: 清，寡婦也，能守其業，用財自衛，不見侵犯。
units.en: Though a widow, Qing maintained her family's enterprise and used her wealth to defend herself, so that no one dared encroach upon her.
units.literal: Qing was a widow who was able to maintain her family's enterprise, using her wealth to protect herself, and was never violated or harmed.

units.zh: 秦皇帝以為貞婦而客之，為筑女懷清臺。
units.en: The First Emperor deemed her a virtuous woman and received her as a guest of honor, building the Terrace of Lady Huaiqing in her name.
units.literal: The First Emperor of Qin considered her a virtuous woman and treated her as an honored guest, building the 'Terrace of the Lady Huaiqing' in her honor.

units.zh: 夫倮鄙人牧長，清窮鄉寡婦，禮抗萬乘，名顯天下，豈非以富邪？
units.en: Luo was but a herdsman of the frontier, and Qing a widow from a remote village, yet both were received with the courtesy due to rulers of ten thousand chariots, and their names resounded throughout the realm. Was this not because of their wealth?
units.literal: Now Luo was a herdsman of the frontier, and Qing a village widow from a remote place, yet in courtesy they were treated as equals of rulers of ten thousand chariots, and their names were known throughout the realm — was this not because of wealth?

units.zh: 漢興，海內為一，開關梁，弛山澤之禁，是以富商大賈周流天下，交易之物莫不通，得其所欲，而徙豪傑諸侯彊族於京師。
units.en: When the Han dynasty arose and the empire was unified, the border passes and bridges were thrown open and the restrictions on the mountains and marshlands relaxed. Great merchants and wealthy traders ranged freely throughout the realm, no commodity was barred from exchange, and each man obtained what he desired. The powerful families and mighty clans of the former feudal states were relocated to the capital.
units.literal: When the Han arose, the empire was unified; the passes and bridges were opened, and the prohibitions on mountains and marshes were relaxed. Thus, wealthy merchants and great traders circulated throughout the realm, and no good was barred from trade; each obtained what he desired. The powerful men, feudal families, and mighty clans were relocated to the capital.

units.zh: 關中自汧、雍以東至河、華，膏壤沃野千里，自虞夏之貢以為上田，而公劉適邠，大王、王季在岐，文王作豐，武王治鎬，故其民猶有先王之遺風，好稼穡，殖五穀，地重，重為邪。
units.en: Within the passes, from Qian and Yong eastward to the Yellow River and Mount Hua, there stretches a thousand li of rich soil and fertile plains — land rated as top grade since the tribute system of Yu and Xia. Gongliu settled at Bin, the Great King and King Ji at Qi, King Wen established Feng, and King Wu governed from Hao. The people of this region still preserve the legacy of those former kings: they love farming, cultivate the five grains, prize the land, and are loath to stray from the right path.
units.literal: Within the passes, from Qian and Yong eastward to the Yellow River and Mount Hua, there stretches a thousand li of rich soil and fertile fields, rated as top-grade land since the tribute system of Yu and Xia. Gongliu settled at Bin, the Great King and King Ji resided at Qi, King Wen founded Feng, and King Wu governed from Hao; therefore its people still preserve the legacy of the former kings — they love farming, cultivate the five grains, value the land, and are reluctant to act improperly.

units.zh: 及秦文、（孝）［德］、繆居雍，隙隴蜀之貨物而多賈。
units.en: When Dukes Wen, De, and Mu of Qin held court at Yong, they profited from the flow of goods between Long and Shu, and merchants were plentiful.
units.literal: When Dukes Wen, De, and Mu of Qin resided at Yong, they exploited the gap in goods between Long and Shu, and there were many merchants.

units.zh: 獻（孝）公徙櫟邑，櫟邑北卻戎翟，東通三晉，亦多大賈。
units.en: Duke Xian relocated to Liyi, which pushed back the Rong and Di to the north and opened trade routes east to the Three Jin states. There too, great merchants abounded.
units.literal: Duke Xian moved to Liyou; Liyou repelled the Rong and Di to the north and connected to the Three Jin to the east, and there too were many great merchants.

units.zh: （武）［孝］、昭治咸陽，因以漢都，長安諸陵，四方輻湊并至而會，地小人眾，故其民益玩巧而事末也。
units.en: Dukes Xiao and Zhao governed from Xianyang, which later became the Han capital. At Chang'an and the surrounding imperial mausoleum towns, people converged from every direction like spokes to a hub. The land was cramped and the population dense, so the people grew ever more devoted to clever craftsmanship and commercial pursuits.
units.literal: Dukes Xiao and Zhao governed from Xianyang, which then became the Han capital; at Chang'an and the various imperial mausoleums, people converged from all four directions like spokes to a hub. The land was small and the population large, so the people grew ever more skilled in cleverness and devoted to commerce.

units.zh: 南則巴蜀。
units.en: To the south lie Ba and Shu.
units.literal: To the south lies Ba and Shu.

units.zh: 巴蜀亦沃野，地饒炧、薑、丹沙、石、銅、鐵、竹、木之器。
units.en: Ba and Shu likewise boast fertile plains. The land is rich in lacquer, ginger, cinnabar, stone, copper, iron, and implements of bamboo and wood.
units.literal: Ba and Shu also have fertile fields, and the land is rich in lacquer, ginger, cinnabar, stone, copper, iron, and implements of bamboo and wood.

units.zh: 南御滇僰，僰僮。
units.en: To the south, they border the Dian and Bo peoples, who supply slaves.
units.literal: To the south they border the Dian and Bo peoples; the Bo provide slaves.

units.zh: 西近邛笮，笮馬、旄牛。
units.en: To the west, they adjoin the Qiong and Zuo peoples, who supply fine horses and yaks.
units.literal: To the west they are close to the Qiong and Zuo peoples, who provide Zuo horses and yaks.

units.zh: 然四塞，棧道千里，無所不通，唯褒斜綰轂其口，以所多易所鮮。
units.en: Though hemmed in on all four sides, the plank roads extend a thousand li and connect to everywhere. Only the Bao and Xie passes serve as the gateway, where the people exchange what they have in abundance for what they lack.
units.literal: Though walled in on four sides, the plank roads extend a thousand li and reach everywhere; only the Bao and Xie passes control the entrance, where they exchange what they have in abundance for what they lack.

units.zh: 天水、隴西、北地、上郡與關中同俗，然西有羌中之利，北有戎翟之畜，畜牧為天下饒。
units.en: Tianshui, Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun share the customs of the region within the passes, but to the west they profit from the Qiang lands, and to the north from the livestock of the Rong and Di. In animal husbandry, they are the richest in the realm.
units.literal: Tianshui, Longxi, Beidi, and Shangjun share the same customs as the region within the passes, yet to the west they enjoy the profits of the Qiang lands, and to the north the livestock of the Rong and Di; in animal husbandry they are the richest in the realm.

units.zh: 然地亦窮險，唯京師要其道。
units.en: Yet the terrain is remote and rugged, and only the capital commands the key routes connecting them.
units.literal: Yet the terrain is also remote and rugged; only the capital commands the routes to them.

units.zh: 故關中之地，於天下三分之一，而人眾不過什三；
units.en: The land within the passes constitutes roughly a third of the realm, and its population amounts to no more than three-tenths of the whole;
units.literal: Therefore, the land within the passes constitutes one-third of the realm, and its population does not exceed three-tenths;

units.zh: 然量其富，什居其六。
units.en: Yet measured by wealth, it accounts for fully six-tenths of the total.
units.literal: yet measured by its wealth, it accounts for six-tenths.

units.zh: 昔唐人都河東，殷人都河內，周人都河南。
units.en: In ancient times, the people of Tang established their capital east of the Yellow River, the Yin within the river's bend, and the Zhou south of the river.
units.literal: In ancient times, the people of Tang had their capital east of the Yellow River, the Yin had theirs within the bend of the river, and the Zhou had theirs south of the river.

units.zh: 夫三河在天下之中，若鼎足，王者所更居也，建國各數百千歲，土地小狹，民人眾，都國諸侯所聚會，故其俗纖儉習事。
units.en: The Three River region sits at the center of the realm, like the three legs of a tripod. Successive kings have made their residence here, and states have endured for hundreds or even thousands of years. The territory is small and cramped, the population dense, and the courts of capitals and feudal lords all converge here. For this reason, the customs of the people are refined, frugal, and practiced in the ways of business.
units.literal: Now the Three River region lies at the center of the realm, like the three legs of a tripod — it is the place where kings have taken turns residing, and states have been established there for hundreds or thousands of years. The territory is small and cramped, the population dense, and the capitals and feudal courts all gather there; therefore its customs are refined, frugal, and practiced in affairs.

units.zh: 楊、平陽陳西賈秦、翟，北賈種、代。
units.en: The people of Yang and Pingyang trade westward with Qin and the Di, and northward with Zhong and Dai.
units.literal: Yang and Pingyang trade westward with Qin and the Di, and northward with Zhong and Dai.

units.zh: 種、代，石北也，地邊胡，數被寇。
units.en: Zhong and Dai lie to the north of the stony lands, bordering the Hu peoples, and suffer frequent raids.
units.literal: Zhong and Dai lie north of the stony land, bordering the Hu peoples, and are frequently raided.

units.zh: 人民矜懻忮，好氣，任俠為姦，不事農商。
units.en: The people are proud, quarrelsome, and hot-tempered. They relish daring exploits, act as knights-errant, and engage in lawless behavior, spurning both farming and commerce.
units.literal: The people are proud, quarrelsome, and contentious; they love spirit, serve as knights-errant and engage in lawlessness, and do not devote themselves to farming or commerce.

units.zh: 然迫近北夷，師旅亟往，中國委輸時有奇羨。
units.en: Yet because they are close to the northern barbarians, armies frequently march through, and the Central States' supply convoys sometimes leave behind unexpected surpluses.
units.literal: Yet being pressed close to the northern barbarians, armies frequently march through, and the Central States supply and transport goods, sometimes leaving surpluses behind.

units.zh: 其民羯羠不均，自全晉之時固已患其僄悍，而武靈王益厲之，其謠俗猶有趙之風也。
units.en: The people are rough and uneven in temperament. Even in the days of united Jin, their fierce and violent spirit was cause for concern, and King Wuling only encouraged it further. Their songs and customs still bear the stamp of Zhao.
units.literal: Their people are coarse and uneven in character; since the time of united Jin, their violence and fierce temper were already a concern, and King Wuling encouraged it further. Their songs and customs still retain the spirit of Zhao.

units.zh: 故楊、平陽陳掾其閒，得所欲。
units.en: And so the merchants of Yang and Pingyang ply their trade among them and obtain whatever they desire.
units.literal: Therefore, the merchants of Yang and Pingyang ply their trade among them and obtain what they desire.

units.zh: 溫、軹西賈上黨，北賈趙、中山。
units.en: The people of Wen and Zhi trade westward with Shangdang and northward with Zhao and Zhongshan.
units.literal: Wen and Zhi trade westward with Shangdang and northward with Zhao and Zhongshan.

units.zh: 中山地薄人眾，猶有沙丘紂淫地餘民，民俗懁急，仰機利而食。
units.en: Zhongshan has thin soil and a dense population, and still harbors remnant populations from Shaqiu, the site of Zhou of Shang's debaucheries. The customs are crafty and impetuous, and the people depend on cunning and profit-seeking for their livelihood.
units.literal: Zhongshan has thin soil and a large population, and still harbors remnants of the people from Shaqiu, the place of Zhou's debauchery. The popular customs are crafty and hasty, and they rely on cunning and profit-seeking for their livelihood.

units.zh: 丈夫相聚游戲，悲歌慨，起則相隨椎剽，休則掘冢作巧姦冶，多美物，為倡優。
units.en: The men gather to amuse themselves, singing songs of bold, impassioned lament. When stirred to action, they band together in gangs to rob and kill; when at rest, they dig up tombs, craft cunning counterfeits and fine trinkets, and work as performers and entertainers.
units.literal: The men gather together to amuse themselves, singing bold and impassioned songs; when active they go about in gangs committing robbery and murder; when idle they dig up tombs and produce cunning counterfeit goods, fine objects, and serve as performers and entertainers.

units.zh: 女子則鼓鳴瑟，跕屣，游媚貴富，入後宮，遍諸侯。
units.en: The women play drums and pluck the zither, trip along in fine slippers, and wander about charming the rich and powerful. They enter the inner palaces and find their way into the courts of feudal lords throughout the realm.
units.literal: The women play drums and pluck the zither, trip along in slippers, and rove about charming the rich and powerful; they enter rear palaces and spread throughout the feudal courts.

units.zh: 然邯鄲亦漳、河之閒一都會也。
units.en: Handan, too, is a great commercial hub situated between the Zhang River and the Yellow River.
units.literal: Now Handan is also a great commercial city between the Zhang River and the Yellow River.

units.zh: 北通燕、涿，南有鄭、衛。
units.en: It opens northward toward Yan and Zhuo, while Zheng and Wei lie to its south.
units.literal: To the north it connects with Yan and Zhuo; to the south lie Zheng and Wei.

units.zh: 鄭、衛俗與趙相類，然近梁、魯，微重而矜節。
units.en: The customs of Zheng and Wei resemble those of Zhao, yet their proximity to Liang and Lu lends them a somewhat weightier character and a greater pride in propriety.
units.literal: The customs of Zheng and Wei are similar to those of Zhao, yet being close to Liang and Lu, they are somewhat more serious and pride themselves on propriety.

units.zh: 濮上之邑徙野王，野王好氣任俠，衛之風也。
units.en: The towns along the Pu River were relocated to Yewang. The people of Yewang love spirited daring and knight-errantry — the very spirit of Wei.
units.literal: The towns along the Pu River were relocated to Yewang; Yewang loves spirited daring and knight-errantry — this is the spirit of Wei.

units.zh: 夫燕亦勃、碣之閒一都會也。
units.en: Yan, too, is a great commercial hub situated between the Gulf of Bohai and Mount Jieshi.
units.literal: Now Yan is also a great commercial city between the Gulf of Bo and Mount Jie.

units.zh: 南通齊、趙，東北邊胡。
units.en: It opens southward toward Qi and Zhao, and on the northeast it borders the Hu peoples.
units.literal: To the south it connects with Qi and Zhao; to the northeast it borders the Hu peoples.

units.zh: 上谷至遼東，地踔遠，人民希，數被寇，大與趙、代俗相類，而民雕捍少慮，有魚鹽棗栗之饒。
units.en: From Shanggu to Liaodong, the territory stretches far into the distance, the population is sparse, and raids are frequent. The customs broadly resemble those of Zhao and Dai — the people are tough, fierce, and reckless. The region abounds in fish, salt, dates, and chestnuts.
units.literal: From Shanggu to Liaodong, the land is remote and far-flung, the population sparse, and frequently raided. The customs are broadly similar to those of Zhao and Dai, and the people are tough, fierce, and heedless. The region has an abundance of fish, salt, dates, and chestnuts.

units.zh: 北鄰烏桓、夫餘，東綰穢貉、朝鮮、真番之利。
units.en: To the north it borders the Wuhuan and Fuyu; to the east it commands the profits of the Huimo, Joseon, and Zhenpan.
units.literal: To the north it borders the Wuhuan and Fuyu peoples; to the east it controls the profits of the Huimo, Joseon, and Zhenpan.

units.zh: 洛陽東賈齊、魯，南賈梁、楚。
units.en: Luoyang conducts trade east with Qi and Lu, and south with Liang and Chu.
units.literal: Luoyang trades eastward with Qi and Lu, and southward with Liang and Chu.

units.zh: 故泰山之陽則魯，其陰則齊。
units.en: The southern slope of Mount Tai belongs to Lu, and the northern slope to Qi.
units.literal: The southern slope of Mount Tai belongs to Lu; its northern slope belongs to Qi.

units.zh: 齊帶山海，膏壤千里，宜桑麻，人民多文綵布帛魚鹽。
units.en: Qi is girded by mountains and sea, with a thousand li of fertile soil ideal for mulberry and hemp. Its people produce a wealth of patterned cloth, silk, fish, and salt.
units.literal: Qi is girded by mountains and sea, with a thousand li of rich soil; it is suited for mulberry and hemp, and its people have an abundance of patterned colored cloth, silk fabrics, fish, and salt.

units.zh: 臨菑亦海岱之閒一都會也。
units.en: Linzi, too, is a great commercial hub situated between the sea and Mount Tai.
units.literal: Linzi is also a great commercial city between the sea and Mount Tai.

units.zh: 其俗寬緩闊達，而足智，好議論，地重，難動搖，怯於眾鬬，勇於持刺，故多劫人者，大國之風也。
units.en: The customs are broad-minded, leisurely, and open. The people are clever, love debate, prize their land, and are difficult to rouse. They are timid in pitched battle but bold when it comes to assassination, and so there are many who resort to robbery. Such is the character of a great state.
units.literal: Its customs are broad-minded, easygoing, and open; the people are full of cleverness, love debate, value the land, and are hard to stir up. They are timid in mass combat but bold at assassination, and therefore there are many who waylay others — such is the character of a great state.

units.zh: 其中具五民。
units.en: All five classes of people are found there.
units.literal: Its population encompasses all five classes of people.

units.zh: 而鄒、魯濱洙、泗，猶有周公遺風，俗好儒，備於禮，故其民齪齪。
units.en: Zou and Lu, along the banks of the Zhu and Si rivers, still preserve the legacy of the Duke of Zhou. Their customs favor Confucian learning and are meticulous in matters of ritual, so the people are careful and diligent.
units.literal: Zou and Lu, situated along the Zhu and Si rivers, still preserve the legacy of the Duke of Zhou; their customs favor Confucian learning and are thorough in ritual, so the people are careful and diligent.

units.zh: 頗有桑麻之業，無林澤之饒。
units.en: They engage in the cultivation of mulberry and hemp, but lack the riches of forests and marshlands.
units.literal: They have a fair amount of mulberry and hemp production, but lack the abundance of forests and marshes.

units.zh: 地小人眾，儉嗇，畏罪遠邪。
units.en: The land is small and the population dense. The people are frugal and thrifty, fearful of punishment, and keep their distance from wrongdoing.
units.literal: The land is small and the population large; they are frugal and thrifty, fear punishment, and shun wrongdoing.

units.zh: 及其衰，好賈趨利，甚於周人。
units.en: But when their fortunes declined, they threw themselves into commerce and the pursuit of profit with an eagerness surpassing even that of the Zhou people.
units.literal: But when their fortunes declined, they took to commerce and pursued profit even more avidly than the people of Zhou.

units.zh: 夫自鴻溝以東，芒、碭以北，屬巨野，此梁、宋也。
units.en: East of the Hong Canal, north of Mang and Dang, stretching to the marshes of Juye — this is the territory of Liang and Song.
units.literal: East of the Hong Canal, north of Mang and Dang, reaching to Juye — this is the region of Liang and Song.

units.zh: 陶、睢陽亦一都會也。
units.en: Tao and Suiyang are likewise great commercial hubs.
units.literal: Tao and Suiyang are also great commercial cities.

units.zh: 昔堯作（游）［於］成陽，舜漁於雷澤，湯止于亳。
units.en: In ancient times, Yao held court at Chengyang, Shun fished at Lei Marsh, and Tang established himself at Bo.
units.literal: In ancient times, Yao resided at Chengyang, Shun fished at Lei Marsh, and Tang settled at Bo.

units.zh: 其俗猶有先王遺風，重厚多君子，好稼穡，雖無山川之饒，能惡衣食，致其蓄藏。
units.en: The customs still preserve the legacy of the former kings. The people are serious and upright, with many gentlemen among them. They love farming, and though the land lacks the riches of mountains and rivers, they willingly wear coarse clothing and eat plain food in order to build up their stores.
units.literal: Its customs still preserve the legacy of the former kings: the people are serious and substantial, with many gentlemen among them. They love farming, and though they lack the riches of mountains and rivers, they are willing to wear coarse clothes and eat plain food in order to build up their stores.

units.zh: 越、楚則有三俗。
units.en: The regions of Yue and Chu can be divided into three distinct zones of custom.
units.literal: Yue and Chu have three distinct sets of customs.

units.zh: 夫自淮北沛、陳、汝南、南郡，此西楚也。
units.en: Pei, Chen, Runan, and Nanjun, north of the Huai — this is the region of Western Chu.
units.literal: From Pei, Chen, Runan, and Nanjun north of the Huai River — this is Western Chu.

units.zh: 其俗剽輕，易發怒，地薄，寡於積聚。
units.en: Its customs are reckless and impetuous, the people quick to anger. The soil is thin, and they accumulate little.
units.literal: Its customs are swift and impetuous; the people are quick to anger. The land is thin and they accumulate little.

units.zh: 江陵故郢都，西通巫、巴，東有雲夢之饒。
units.en: Jiangling, the former Ying capital, connects westward to Wu and Ba, and to the east commands the riches of the Yunmeng marshlands.
units.literal: Jiangling is the former Ying capital; to the west it connects with Wu and Ba, and to the east it has the riches of the Yunmeng marshes.

units.zh: 陳在楚夏之交，通魚鹽之貨，其民多賈。
units.en: Chen sits at the intersection of Chu and the Xia region, channeling the trade in fish and salt. Its people are overwhelmingly merchants.
units.literal: Chen sits at the intersection of Chu and the Xia region, trading in fish and salt; its people are largely merchants.

units.zh: 徐、僮、取慮，則清刻，矜己諾。
units.en: The people of Xu, Tong, and Qulü are sharp and exacting, taking great pride in keeping their word.
units.literal: Xu, Tong, and Qulü are sharp and exacting, proud of keeping their word.

units.zh: 彭城以東，東海、吳、廣陵，此東楚也。
units.en: From Pengcheng eastward to Donghai, Wu, and Guangling — this is the region of Eastern Chu.
units.literal: From Pengcheng eastward to Donghai, Wu, and Guangling — this is Eastern Chu.

units.zh: 其俗類徐、僮。
units.en: Its customs are akin to those of Xu and Tong.
units.literal: Its customs resemble those of Xu and Tong.

units.zh: 朐、繒以北，俗則齊。
units.en: North of Qu and Zeng, the customs follow those of Qi.
units.literal: North of Qu and Zeng, the customs are those of Qi.

units.zh: 浙江南則越。
units.en: South of the Zhe River lies Yue.
units.literal: South of the Zhe River lies Yue.

units.zh: 夫吳自闔廬、春申、王濞三人招致天下之喜游子弟，東有海鹽之饒，章山之銅，三江、五湖之利，亦江東一都會也。
units.en: Ever since Helü, Lord Chunshen, and King Bi attracted ambitious young men from across the realm, Wu has enjoyed the riches of seaside salt to the east, the copper of Mount Zhang, and the profits of the Three Rivers and Five Lakes. It, too, is a great commercial hub east of the Yangtze.
units.literal: Wu, ever since the three men — Helü, Lord Chunshen, and King Bi — attracted wandering youths from throughout the realm, has enjoyed the riches of seaside salt to the east, the copper of Mount Zhang, and the profits of the Three Rivers and Five Lakes; it too is a great commercial hub east of the Yangtze.

units.zh: 衡山、九江、江南、豫章、長沙，是南楚也，其俗大類西楚。
units.en: Hengshan, Jiujiang, Jiangnan, Yuzhang, and Changsha — this is the region of Southern Chu. Its customs are broadly similar to those of Western Chu.
units.literal: Hengshan, Jiujiang, Jiangnan, Yuzhang, and Changsha — this is Southern Chu. Its customs are broadly similar to those of Western Chu.

units.zh: 郢之後徙壽春，亦一都會也。
units.en: After the Chu capital was relocated from Ying to Shouchun, Shouchun too became a great commercial hub.
units.literal: After the capital was moved from Ying to Shouchun, Shouchun also became a great commercial city.

units.zh: 而合肥受南北潮，皮革、鮑、木輸會也。
units.en: Hefei receives the tides of commerce from both north and south, serving as a gathering point for hides, salted fish, and timber.
units.literal: And Hefei receives the tides of commerce from north and south — it is a gathering point for leather hides, salted fish, and timber.

units.zh: 與閩中、干越雜俗，故南楚好辭，巧說少信。
units.en: The customs mingle with those of Min and Gan-Yue. For this reason, the people of Southern Chu are fond of fine words and skilled in persuasion, but lacking in trustworthiness.
units.literal: It mingles with the customs of Min and Gan-Yue, and so Southern Chu is fond of eloquence, skilled in persuasion, but lacking in trustworthiness.

units.zh: 江南卑溼，丈夫早夭。
units.en: South of the Yangtze, the land is low and damp, and men tend to die young.
units.literal: South of the Yangtze the land is low and damp, and men die young.

units.zh: 多竹木。
units.en: Bamboo and timber are plentiful.
units.literal: There is an abundance of bamboo and wood.

units.zh: 豫章出黃金，長沙出連、錫，然堇堇物之所有，取之不足以更費。
units.en: Yuzhang produces gold, and Changsha yields lead and tin, but the deposits are so meager that the cost of extraction barely justifies the effort.
units.literal: Yuzhang produces gold, and Changsha produces lead and tin, but these resources are so meager that extracting them barely covers the cost.

units.zh: 九疑、蒼梧以南至儋耳者，與江南大同俗，而楊越多焉。
units.en: From Jiuyi and Cangwu southward all the way to Dan'er, the customs broadly resemble those south of the Yangtze, but with a stronger Yang-Yue character.
units.literal: From Jiuyi and Cangwu southward to Dan'er, the customs are broadly the same as south of the Yangtze, but with more Yang-Yue elements.

units.zh: 番禺亦其一都會也，珠璣、犀、瑁、果、布之湊。
units.en: Panyu, too, is a great commercial hub of the region — a gathering point for pearls, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, fruit, and cloth.
units.literal: Panyu is also a great commercial city among them — a gathering point for pearls, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, fruit, and cloth.

units.zh: 潁川、南陽，夏人之居也。
units.en: Yingchuan and Nanyang are the ancestral homeland of the Xia people.
units.literal: Yingchuan and Nanyang are the homeland of the Xia people.

units.zh: 夏人政尚忠樸，猶有先王之遺風。
units.en: The Xia people esteem loyalty and simplicity in governance, still preserving the legacy of the former kings.
units.literal: The Xia people in governance esteem loyalty and simplicity, and still preserve the legacy of the former kings.

units.zh: 潁川敦願。
units.en: The people of Yingchuan are plain, sincere, and earnest.
units.literal: The people of Yingchuan are sincere and earnest.

units.zh: 秦末世，遷不軌之民於南陽。
units.en: In the waning days of the Qin, lawless people were relocated to Nanyang.
units.literal: In the last days of Qin, lawless people were relocated to Nanyang.

units.zh: 南陽西通武關、鄖關，東南受漢、江、淮。
units.en: Nanyang connects westward to the Wuguan and Yun passes, and to the southeast receives the commerce of the Han, Yangtze, and Huai rivers.
units.literal: Nanyang connects westward to Wuguan and Yunguan passes, and to the southeast receives the trade of the Han, Yangtze, and Huai rivers.

units.zh: 宛亦一都會也。
units.en: Wan, too, is a great commercial hub.
units.literal: Wan is also a great commercial city.

units.zh: 俗雜好事，業多賈。
units.en: The customs are mixed and the people love enterprise. Commerce predominates among their occupations.
units.literal: Its customs are mixed, and the people love enterprise; commerce predominates among their occupations.

units.zh: 其任俠，交通潁川，故至今謂之「夏人」。
units.en: Their tradition of knight-errantry and their connections with Yingchuan explain why they are still called 'Xia people' to this day.
units.literal: Their knight-errantry and connections with Yingchuan explain why to this day they are called 'Xia people.'

units.zh: 夫天下物所鮮所多，人民謠俗，山東食海鹽，山西食鹽鹵，領南、沙北固往往出鹽，大體如此矣。
units.en: As for the distribution of scarcity and abundance throughout the realm, and the customs and character of the people: east of the mountains they eat sea salt, west of the mountains they eat rock salt, and south of the passes and north of the deserts salt is produced in scattered locations. Such, in broad outline, is the picture.
units.literal: Now, regarding where things are scarce and where they are abundant throughout the realm, and the customs and songs of the people: east of the mountains they eat sea salt, west of the mountains they eat rock salt; south of the mountain passes and north of the deserts, salt is produced here and there. In broad outline, this is how it stands.

units.zh: 總之，楚越之地，地廣人希，飯稻羹魚，或火耕而水耨，果隋蠃蛤，不待賈而足，地埶饒食，無饑饉之患，以故呰窳偷生，無積聚而多貧。
units.en: In sum, the lands of Chu and Yue are vast and thinly populated. The people eat rice and fish soup, practice slash-and-burn farming with flooded weeding, and gather wild fruits, snails, and clams — all sufficient without the need for trade. The land's natural bounty ensures plentiful food with no fear of famine. And so the people live idly, from hand to mouth, laying up no stores, and many remain poor.
units.literal: In sum, in the lands of Chu and Yue, the territory is vast and the population sparse. They eat rice and fish soup, practice slash-and-burn agriculture with flooded weeding, and gather fruits, snails, and clams. They have enough without needing trade. The land's natural bounty ensures food is plentiful and there is no fear of famine. For this reason, the people are idle and lazy, living from hand to mouth, with no stores laid up and much poverty.

units.zh: 是故江淮以南，無凍餓之人，亦無千金之家。
units.en: And so south of the Yangtze and the Huai, no one freezes or starves, yet neither are there any families worth a thousand in gold.
units.literal: Therefore, south of the Yangtze and Huai, there are no people who freeze or starve, nor are there any families worth a thousand in gold.

units.zh: 沂、泗水以北，宜五穀桑麻六畜，地小人眾，數被水旱之害，民好畜藏，故秦、夏、梁、魯好農而重民。
units.en: North of the Yi and Si rivers, the land is suited to the five grains, mulberry, hemp, and the six domestic animals. The territory is small, the population large, and floods and droughts are frequent. The people are keen to accumulate savings, and so the regions of Qin, Xia, Liang, and Lu prize agriculture and value the people.
units.literal: North of the Yi and Si rivers, the land is suitable for the five grains, mulberry, hemp, and the six domestic animals. The territory is small and the population large, frequently afflicted by floods and droughts. The people love to store up savings; therefore the regions of Qin, Xia, Liang, and Lu love agriculture and value their people.

units.zh: 三河、宛、陳亦然，加以商賈。
units.en: The Three Rivers, Wan, and Chen follow the same pattern, with commerce added to the mix.
units.literal: The Three Rivers region, Wan, and Chen are the same, with the addition of commerce.

units.zh: 齊、趙設智巧，仰機利。
units.en: Qi and Zhao employ cleverness and ingenuity, relying on opportunism and profit.
units.literal: Qi and Zhao employ cleverness and ingenuity, relying on opportunity and profit.

units.zh: 燕、代田畜而事蠶。
units.en: Yan and Dai farm, raise livestock, and practice sericulture.
units.literal: Yan and Dai farm and raise livestock, and engage in sericulture.

units.zh: 由此觀之，賢人深謀於廊廟，論議朝廷，守信死節隱居巖穴之士設為名高者安歸乎？
units.en: Seen from this vantage point, worthy men plot in the corridors of the court and debate in the audience hall. Gentlemen keep faith unto death, uphold their integrity, and hide away in mountain caves, cultivating lofty reputations — but to what do they all return in the end?
units.literal: Viewed from this perspective — the worthy men who plot deeply in the corridors of the court, who debate in the audience hall, the gentlemen who keep faith unto death, maintain their integrity, and hide in mountain caves, establishing themselves as men of lofty reputation — to what do they all return?

units.zh: 歸於富厚也。
units.en: They return, in the end, to wealth and abundance.
units.literal: They return to wealth and abundance.

units.zh: 是以廉吏久，久更富，廉賈歸富。
units.en: And so an honest official who serves long enough eventually grows rich, and an honest merchant in the end grows wealthy.
units.literal: Therefore, an honest official who serves long enough eventually grows rich, and an honest merchant ultimately becomes wealthy.

units.zh: 富者，人之情性，所不學而俱欲者也。
units.en: The desire for wealth is rooted in human nature. It is something all men crave without ever having to be taught.
units.literal: Wealth is something rooted in human nature — something all desire without needing to be taught.

units.zh: 故壯士在軍，攻城先登，陷陣卻敵，斬將搴旗，前蒙矢石，不避湯火之難者，為重賞使也。
units.en: And so brave soldiers are first to scale the walls in an assault, smash through enemy lines, cut down generals, and seize their banners. They charge into showers of arrows and stones without flinching from fire or boiling water because they are driven by the promise of lavish rewards.
units.literal: Therefore, brave soldiers in the army who are the first to scale the walls in an assault, who break through enemy lines, cut down generals and seize banners, who rush forward into arrows and stones and do not shrink from boiling water or raging fire — they do so because they are driven by the promise of lavish rewards.

units.zh: 其在閭巷少年，攻剽椎埋，劫人作姦，掘冢鑄幣，任俠并兼，借交報仇，篡逐幽隱，不避法禁，走死地如騖者，其實皆為財用耳。
units.en: As for the young ruffians of the back alleys — those who rob and murder, waylay travelers, forge coins and dig up graves, act as knights-errant swallowing up rivals, borrow connections to exact revenge, and carry out covert schemes in the shadows, defying every law and prohibition, rushing toward their own deaths as eagerly as ducks taking flight — in truth, they do it all for the sake of money.
units.literal: As for the young men of the alleys and lanes who rob and murder, waylay and commit crimes, dig up graves and forge coins, act as knights-errant absorbing smaller rivals, avenge wrongs through borrowed connections, usurp and pursue in dark concealment, defying all laws and prohibitions, rushing toward death as eagerly as ducks taking to water — in truth, they all do so for the sake of wealth.

units.zh: 今夫趙女鄭姬，設形容，揳鳴琴，揄長袂，躡利屣，目挑心招，出不遠千里，不擇老少者，奔富厚也。
units.en: Consider the beauties of Zhao and the maidens of Zheng. They adorn their faces, take up the singing zither, trail their long sleeves, and trip along in fine slippers, beckoning with glances and luring with their hearts. They will travel a thousand li, caring nothing whether a man is old or young — all for the sake of wealth.
units.literal: Now consider the beauties of Zhao and the maidens of Zheng: they adorn their faces, set aside their singing zithers, trail their long sleeves, and trip along in fine slippers, beckoning with their eyes and luring with their hearts, traveling a thousand li without regard for whether a man is old or young — all for the sake of running toward wealth.

units.zh: 游閒公子，飾冠劍，連車騎，亦為富貴容也。
units.en: The idle young lords who adorn their caps and swords and parade about in linked carriages with mounted escorts do so to put on the trappings of wealth and nobility.
units.literal: The idle young lords who adorn their caps and swords and parade in linked carriages and mounted escorts also do so to display the appearance of wealth and nobility.

units.zh: 弋射漁獵，犯晨夜，冒霜雪，馳阬谷，不避猛獸之害，為得味也。
units.en: Those who hunt with bow and arrow, fish, and track game, braving the dawn and the night, enduring frost and snow, galloping through ravines and valleys without shrinking from the danger of fierce beasts — they do it all for the sake of fine flavors.
units.literal: Those who hunt with arrows, fish, and pursue game, braving the dawn and night, enduring frost and snow, galloping through ravines and valleys, not shrinking from the danger of fierce beasts — they do so for the sake of obtaining fine flavors.

units.zh: 博戲馳逐，鬬雞走狗，作色相矜，必爭勝者，重失負也。
units.en: Gamblers, racers, cockfighters, and dog-racers, putting on airs and vying with one another, always insisting on winning — they act this way because they dread losing.
units.literal: Those who gamble, race, cockfight, and dog-race, putting on airs and boasting to each other, insisting on winning — they do so because they dread losing.

units.zh: 醫方諸食技術之人，焦神極能，為重糈也。
units.en: Physicians, herbalists, diviners, cooks, and skilled artisans who burn through their mental energies and push their abilities to the limit do so for the sake of generous compensation.
units.literal: Physicians, herbalists, diviners, cooks, and skilled artisans who burn their spirits and exhaust their abilities — they do so for the sake of generous compensation.

units.zh: 吏士舞文弄法，刻章偽書，不避刀鋸之誅者，沒於賂遺也。
units.en: Officials and clerks who twist documents and toy with the law, forge seals and fabricate records, unafraid of execution by blade or saw — they are lured by bribery and gifts.
units.literal: Officials and clerks who manipulate documents and toy with the law, forge seals and fabricate documents, not shrinking from execution by blade or saw — they are sunk in bribery and gifts.

units.zh: 農工商賈畜長，固求富益貨也。
units.en: Farmers, artisans, merchants, traders, and herders — all of them naturally seek to grow rich and multiply their goods.
units.literal: Farmers, artisans, merchants, traders, and herders — all naturally seek to grow rich and increase their goods.

units.zh: 此有知盡能索耳，終不餘力而讓財矣。
units.en: In every case, people exhaust their knowledge and abilities in the pursuit of gain. In the end, no one holds back strength or yields wealth to another.
units.literal: In all these cases, people exhaust their knowledge and abilities in pursuit of gain; in the end, none holds back his strength or yields his wealth to another.

units.zh: 諺曰：「百里不販樵，千里不販糴。」
units.en: As the proverb goes: 'Don't haul firewood a hundred li to sell, and don't haul grain a thousand li to sell.'
units.literal: The proverb says: 'Don't sell firewood over a hundred li, and don't sell grain over a thousand li.'

units.zh: 居之一歲，種之以穀；
units.en: If you settle in a place for a year, plant grain;
units.literal: If you dwell in a place for one year, plant grain;

units.zh: 十歲，樹之以木；
units.en: If for ten years, plant trees;
units.literal: if for ten years, plant trees;

units.zh: 百歲，來之以德。
units.en: If for a hundred years, draw people through virtue.
units.literal: if for a hundred years, attract people through virtue.

units.zh: 德者，人物之謂也。
units.en: By 'virtue' is meant the attraction of people and goods.
units.literal: 'Virtue' here refers to people and goods.

units.zh: 今有無秩祿之奉，爵邑之入，而樂與之比者。
units.en: Now there are those who receive no official salary, no income from noble rank or landed fief, yet are happy to live on a par with those who do.
units.literal: Now there are those who receive no official salary or stipend, no income from noble rank or fief, and yet are content to compare themselves favorably with those who do.

units.zh: 命曰「素封」。
units.en: They are called the 'Commoner Lords' — men enfeoffed by nothing but their own wealth.
units.literal: These are called 'plain enfeoffed' — commoner lords.

units.zh: 封者食租稅，歲率戶二百。
units.en: An enfeoffed lord lives on rent and taxes, collecting roughly two hundred cash per household per year.
units.literal: An enfeoffed lord lives on rent and taxes, at a rate of roughly two hundred cash per household per year.

units.zh: 千戶之君則二十萬，朝覲聘享出其中。
units.en: A lord of a thousand households thus takes in two hundred thousand cash, from which he pays for court audiences, tribute missions, and banquets.
units.literal: A lord of a thousand households thus receives two hundred thousand, from which court audiences, tribute gifts, and banquets are funded.

units.zh: 庶民農工商賈，率亦歲萬息二千，百萬之家則二十萬，而更傜租賦出其中。
units.en: For commoners — farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders — the rate of return is generally two thousand per ten thousand of capital per year. A household worth a million thus earns two hundred thousand, from which corvée duties, rent, and taxes must be paid.
units.literal: For commoners — farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders — the rate is generally two thousand cash interest per ten thousand of capital per year. A household worth a million thus earns two hundred thousand, from which corvée labor, rent, and taxes are paid.

units.zh: 衣食之欲，恣所好美矣。
units.en: They indulge their desires for fine clothing and food to the fullest.
units.literal: Their desires for clothing and food are indulged in whatever they find fine and beautiful.

units.zh: 故曰陸地牧馬二百蹄，牛蹄角千，千足羊，澤中千足彘，水居千石魚陂，山居千章之材。
units.en: Thus, it is said: on dry land, a herd of fifty horses, a thousand head of cattle, a thousand sheep; in the marshlands, a thousand pigs; on the waters, a fishpond yielding a thousand shi; in the mountains, a stand of a thousand timber trunks.
units.literal: Therefore, it is said: on dry land, herding two hundred hooves of horses, a thousand hooves and horns of cattle, a thousand feet of sheep; in the marshes, a thousand feet of pigs; on the water, a fish pond of a thousand shi; in the mountains, a thousand trunks of timber.

units.zh: 安邑千樹棗；
units.en: In Anyi, a thousand date trees;
units.literal: In Anyi, a thousand date trees;

units.zh: 燕、秦千樹栗；
units.en: In Yan and Qin, a thousand chestnut trees;
units.literal: in Yan and Qin, a thousand chestnut trees;

units.zh: 蜀、漢、江陵千樹橘；
units.en: In Shu, Han, and Jiangling, a thousand orange trees;
units.literal: in Shu, Han, and Jiangling, a thousand orange trees;

units.zh: 淮北、常山已南，河濟之閒千樹萩；
units.en: North of the Huai and south of Changshan, between the Yellow River and the Ji, a thousand catalpa trees;
units.literal: north of the Huai and south of Changshan, between the Yellow River and the Ji, a thousand catalpa trees;

units.zh: 陳、夏千畝漆；
units.en: In Chen and Xia, a thousand mu of lacquer trees;
units.literal: in Chen and Xia, a thousand mu of lacquer trees;

units.zh: 齊、魯千畝桑麻；
units.en: In Qi and Lu, a thousand mu of mulberry and hemp;
units.literal: in Qi and Lu, a thousand mu of mulberry and hemp;

units.zh: 渭川千畝竹；
units.en: Along the Wei River, a thousand mu of bamboo;
units.literal: along the Wei River, a thousand mu of bamboo;

units.zh: 及名國萬家之城，帶郭千畝畝鐘之田，若千畝卮茜，千畦薑韭：此其人皆與千戶侯等。
units.en: And near a famous capital or a city of ten thousand households, a thousand mu of highly productive fields adjoining the outer walls, or a thousand mu of madder and gardenia, or a thousand plots of ginger and chives. The owner of these is the equal of a lord enfeoffed with a thousand households.
units.literal: and in a famous state or a city of ten thousand households, a thousand mu of fields yielding a zhong per mu adjacent to the outer walls, or a thousand mu of madder and gardenia, or a thousand plots of ginger and chives — the owner of any of these is the equal of a lord of a thousand households.

units.zh: 然是富給之資也，不窺市井，不行異邑，坐而待收，身有處士之義而取給焉。
units.en: These are the assets that supply wealth effortlessly. One need not peer into the marketplace or travel to distant cities — simply sit and wait for the harvest to come in. One preserves the dignity of a retired gentleman while drawing a comfortable livelihood.
units.literal: Yet these are the assets that provide effortless wealth: one need not peer into the marketplace or travel to other cities, but simply sit and wait for the harvest. One maintains the dignity of a retired gentleman while drawing one's sustenance.

units.zh: 若至家貧親老，妻子軟弱，歲時無以祭祀進醵，飲食被服不足以自通，如此不慚恥，則無所比矣。
units.en: But if one's family is poor and one's parents elderly, one's wife and children frail, and at the seasonal festivals one cannot afford sacrifices and contributions, and one's food and clothing are insufficient to maintain appearances — if a man feels no shame at this, he is truly beyond all comparison.
units.literal: But if one's household is poor and one's parents are old, one's wife and children weak, and at the seasonal festivals one cannot afford to make sacrifices and contributions, and one's food, drink, and clothing are insufficient to maintain appearances — if one feels no shame at this, then one is truly beyond comparison.

units.zh: 是以無財作力，少有鬬智，既饒爭時，此其大經也。
units.en: And so when a man has nothing, he labors with his body. When he has a little, he contends with his wits. When already wealthy, he competes through timing. This is the guiding principle.
units.literal: Therefore, when one has no wealth, one works with physical strength; when one has a little, one contends with cleverness; when already well-off, one competes through timing. This is the broad principle.

units.zh: 今治生不待危身取給，則賢人勉焉。
units.en: If managing one's livelihood does not require risking life and limb, then worthy men should strive at it.
units.literal: Now if managing one's livelihood does not require endangering one's person to earn a living, then worthy men should exert themselves at it.

units.zh: 是故本富為上，末富次之，姦富最下。
units.en: Therefore, wealth earned through the primary occupations ranks highest, wealth from commerce ranks next, and wealth gained through wrongdoing ranks lowest of all.
units.literal: Therefore, wealth from the primary occupations is the highest; wealth from commerce is next; and wealth from wrongdoing is the lowest.

units.zh: 無巖處奇士之行，而長貧賤，好語仁義，亦足羞也。
units.en: To lack the conduct of a hermit dwelling among the crags, yet to remain poor and lowly for a lifetime while mouthing talk of benevolence and righteousness — this too is cause for shame.
units.literal: If one does not possess the conduct of a recluse dwelling in mountain caves, yet remains poor and lowly for a lifetime while delighting in talk of benevolence and righteousness — this too is cause for shame.

units.zh: 凡編戶之民，富相什則卑下之，伯則畏憚之，千則役，萬則仆，物之理也。
units.en: Among registered householders, if one man is ten times richer than another, the poorer defers; a hundred times, and the poorer fears him; a thousand times, and the poorer serves him; ten thousand times, and the poorer becomes his slave. Such is the way of things.
units.literal: Among the registered householders, if one man is ten times richer than another, the poorer man defers to him; if a hundred times, he fears him; if a thousand times, he serves him; if ten thousand times, he becomes his slave. This is the natural order of things.

units.zh: 夫用貧求富，農不如工，工不如商，刺繡文不如倚市門，此言末業，貧者之資也。
units.en: When the poor seek wealth, farming is less profitable than craftsmanship, and craftsmanship less profitable than commerce. Embroidering fine patterns is less rewarding than leaning against the marketplace gate. This refers to the secondary occupations — the means by which the poor lift themselves up.
units.literal: Now, in using poverty to seek wealth, farming is not as good as craftsmanship, craftsmanship not as good as commerce; embroidering fine patterns is not as good as leaning against the marketplace gate. This refers to the secondary occupations — the capital resources of the poor.

units.zh: 通邑大都，酤一歲千釀，醯醬千瓨，漿千甔，屠牛羊彘千皮，販穀糶千鐘，薪槁千車，船長千丈，木千章，竹竿萬，其軺車百乘，牛車千兩，木器髤者千枚，銅器千鈞，素木鐵器若炧茜千石，馬蹄蹾千，牛千足，羊彘千雙，僮手指千，筋角丹沙千斤，其帛絮細布千鈞，文采千匹，榻布皮革千石，漆千斗，糱麹鹽豉千荅，鮐鮆千斤，鯫千石，鮑千鈞，棗栗千石者三之，狐鼦裘千皮，羔羊裘千石，旃席千具，佗果菜千鐘，子貸金錢千貫，節駔會，貪賈三之，廉賈五之，此亦比千乘之家，其大率也。
units.en: In a great commercial metropolis: a wine brewer making a thousand batches a year, a vinegar and sauce merchant with a thousand jars, a beverage seller with a thousand casks, a butcher with a thousand hides, a grain trader with a thousand zhong, a firewood dealer with a thousand cartloads, a shipowner with a thousand zhang of vessel, a timber dealer with a thousand trunks, a bamboo dealer with ten thousand poles — or a hundred light carriages, a thousand ox-carts, a thousand lacquered wooden wares, a thousand jun of bronze vessels, a thousand shi of plain wood and iron wares or of lacquer and madder, a thousand hooves of horses, a thousand head of cattle, a thousand pairs of sheep and pigs, a thousand slaves, a thousand jin of sinew, horn, or cinnabar, a thousand jun of silk floss and fine cloth, a thousand bolts of patterned fabric, a thousand shi of coarse cloth and leather, a thousand dou of lacquer, a thousand da of malt, yeast, salt, or soy, a thousand jin of mackerel and shad, a thousand shi of small fish, a thousand jun of salted fish, three thousand shi of dates and chestnuts, a thousand fox and sable furs, a thousand shi of lamb furs, a thousand sets of felt mats, a thousand zhong of other fruits and vegetables, or a thousand strings of cash at interest — all with timely brokering. An aggressive merchant turns his capital three times a year; a conservative one, five. All these are comparable to the wealth of a family of a thousand chariots. This is the general standard.
