units.literal: In a great commercial city or metropolis: a wine seller brewing a thousand batches a year; a vinegar and sauce seller with a thousand jars; a seller of beverages with a thousand casks; a butcher of cattle, sheep, and pigs with a thousand hides; a grain trader with a thousand zhong; a firewood dealer with a thousand carts; a shipowner with a thousand zhang of vessel; a timber dealer with a thousand trunks; a bamboo dealer with ten thousand poles; light carriages numbering a hundred; ox-carts numbering a thousand; lacquered wooden wares numbering a thousand; bronze vessels weighing a thousand jun; plain wood and iron wares or lacquer and madder weighing a thousand shi; horses numbering a thousand hooves; cattle numbering a thousand feet; sheep and pigs numbering a thousand pairs; slaves numbering a thousand fingers; sinew, horn, and cinnabar weighing a thousand jin; silk floss and fine cloth weighing a thousand jun; patterned fabrics numbering a thousand bolts; coarse cloth and leather weighing a thousand shi; lacquer numbering a thousand dou; malt, yeast, salt, and soy numbering a thousand da; mackerel and shad weighing a thousand jin; small fish numbering a thousand shi; salted fish weighing a thousand jun; dates and chestnuts at a thousand shi three times over; fox and sable furs numbering a thousand skins; lamb furs at a thousand shi; felt mats numbering a thousand sets; other fruits and vegetables at a thousand zhong; money-lending at a thousand strings of cash — all with timely brokering, aggressive merchants turning the capital three times a year, conservative merchants five times. All these are comparable to a family of a thousand chariots. This is the general standard.

units.zh: 佗雜業不中什二，則非吾財也。
units.en: Any other miscellaneous trade that does not yield at least a twenty percent return is not worth the investment.
units.literal: Any other miscellaneous business that does not yield at least twenty percent is not worth my money.

units.zh: 請略道當世千里之中，賢人所以富者，令後世得以觀擇焉。
units.en: Allow me now to briefly recount how the worthy men of the present age have built their fortunes, so that future generations may examine their examples and learn from them.
units.literal: Allow me to briefly describe how the worthy men of the present age, within a thousand li, have achieved their wealth, so that later generations may observe and draw lessons from their examples.

units.zh: 蜀卓氏之先，趙人也，用鐵冶富。
units.en: The ancestors of the Zhuo family of Shu were originally from Zhao and had grown wealthy through iron smelting.
units.literal: The ancestors of the Zhuo family of Shu were originally people of Zhao, who grew wealthy through iron smelting.

units.zh: 秦破趙，遷卓氏。
units.en: When Qin conquered Zhao, the Zhuo family was among those relocated.
units.literal: When Qin conquered Zhao, the Zhuo family was relocated.

units.zh: 卓氏見虜略，獨夫妻推輦，行詣遷處。
units.en: Stripped of everything, Zhuo and his wife alone pushed a handcart and walked to the designated resettlement.
units.literal: The Zhuo family, having been captured and dispossessed, set out as just husband and wife, pushing a handcart, and walked to the place of relocation.

units.zh: 諸遷虜少有餘財，爭與吏，求近處，處葭萌。
units.en: Among the other relocatees, those who still had some money left competed to bribe the officials, petitioning to be settled nearby, at Jiameng.
units.literal: Among the relocated captives, those with a little remaining wealth competed to bribe the officials, requesting to be placed nearby, and settled at Jiameng.

units.zh: 唯卓氏曰：「此地狹薄。
units.en: Only the Zhuo patriarch said: 'This land is cramped and barren.
units.literal: Only the Zhuo family said: 'This place is narrow and barren.

units.zh: 吾聞汶山之下，沃野，下有蹲鴟，至死不饑。
units.en: I hear that at the foot of Mount Wen lie fertile plains, and beneath the soil grows taro — enough to keep one fed for a lifetime.
units.literal: I have heard that below Mount Wen there are fertile plains, and underground there are taro plants — one need never go hungry.

units.zh: 民工於市，易賈。」
units.en: The people are clever at commerce, and trade flows easily.'
units.literal: The people are skilled in the marketplace, and trade is easy.'

units.zh: 乃求遠遷。
units.en: And so he petitioned to be sent to a more distant site.
units.literal: So he requested to be sent to a distant location.

units.zh: 致之臨邛，大喜，即鐵山鼓鑄，運籌策，傾滇蜀之民，富至僮千人。
units.en: He was sent to Linqiong and was overjoyed. He set about smelting iron from the nearby mountains, devising shrewd strategies, and attracting the people of Dian and Shu until his fortune grew to encompass a thousand slaves.
units.literal: He was sent to Linqiong and was overjoyed. He immediately began smelting iron from the mountains, devising strategies and calculations, attracting the people of Dian and Shu, until his wealth grew to include a thousand slaves.

units.zh: 田池射獵之樂，擬於人君。
units.en: His pleasures in country estates, fishponds, archery, and hunting rivaled those of a sovereign.
units.literal: His pleasures in fields, ponds, archery, and hunting rivaled those of a sovereign.

units.zh: 程鄭，山東遷虜也，亦冶鑄，賈椎髻之民，富埒卓氏，俱居臨邛。
units.en: Cheng Zheng was a relocated captive from east of the mountains who also engaged in iron smelting and traded with the mallet-coiffed peoples. His wealth rivaled that of the Zhuo family, and both resided at Linqiong.
units.literal: Cheng Zheng was a relocated captive from east of the mountains. He too engaged in iron smelting and traded with the mallet-coiffed peoples, amassing wealth rivaling the Zhuo family. They both resided at Linqiong.

units.zh: 宛孔氏之先，梁人也，用鐵冶為業。
units.en: The ancestors of the Kong family of Wan were originally from Liang, where they made iron smelting their trade.
units.literal: The ancestors of the Kong family of Wan were people of Liang who made iron smelting their trade.

units.zh: 秦伐魏，遷孔氏南陽。
units.en: When Qin conquered Wei, the Kong family was relocated to Nanyang.
units.literal: When Qin attacked Wei, the Kong family was relocated to Nanyang.

units.zh: 大鼓鑄，規陂池，連車騎，游諸侯，因通商賈之利，有游閒公子之賜與名。
units.en: They expanded their foundries, developed reservoirs and fishponds, and traveled among the feudal lords with trains of carriages and riders. The profits of trade gave them the generosity and reputation of leisured young gentlemen.
units.literal: They greatly expanded their smelting works, developed reservoirs and ponds, maintained trains of carriages and riders, traveled among the feudal lords, and through the profits of trade acquired the generosity and reputation of leisured young gentlemen.

units.zh: 然其贏得過當，愈於纖嗇，家致富數千金，故南陽行賈盡法孔氏之雍容。
units.en: Their profits far surpassed the returns of miserly saving. The family amassed several thousand in gold, and Nanyang's traveling merchants all imitated the Kong clan's easy elegance.
units.literal: Yet their profits exceeded their investment and surpassed the gains of meticulous thrift. The family amassed several thousand in gold, so all the traveling merchants of Nanyang imitated the Kong clan's easy elegance.

units.zh: 魯人俗儉嗇，而曹邴氏尤甚，以鐵冶起，富至巨萬。
units.en: The people of Lu are by custom frugal and thrifty, and the Bing family of Cao was the most extreme case. They rose through iron smelting and amassed an enormous fortune.
units.literal: The people of Lu are customarily frugal and thrifty, and the Bing family of Cao was especially so. They rose through iron smelting and grew wealthy to the tune of enormous sums.

units.zh: 然家自父兄子孫約，俛有拾，仰有取，貰貸行賈遍郡國。
units.en: Yet from father and elder brother down to sons and grandsons, the family rule was strict economy: bending down, one picks up whatever is found; looking up, one takes whatever is available. They extended credit and traded across the commanderies and kingdoms.
units.literal: Yet within the family, from father and elder brother to sons and grandsons, the rule was strict economy: look down and you pick up what you find; look up and you take what you can. They extended credit and traded throughout the commanderies and kingdoms.

units.zh: 鄒、魯以其故多去文學而趨利者，以曹邴氏也。
units.en: The reason so many in Zou and Lu abandoned scholarly pursuits and rushed after profit was the example of the Bing family of Cao.
units.literal: The reason many people of Zou and Lu abandoned scholarship and rushed toward profit was because of the Bing family of Cao.

units.zh: 齊俗賤奴虜，而刀閒獨愛貴之。
units.en: In Qi, custom held slaves and captives in contempt, but Dao Jian alone valued and cherished them.
units.literal: The customs of Qi disdain slaves and captives, but Dao Jian alone valued and cherished them.

units.zh: 桀黠奴，人之所患也，唯刀閒收取，使之逐漁鹽商賈之利，或連車騎，交守相，然愈益任之。
units.en: Cunning and unruly slaves are the bane of most men. Yet Dao Jian alone took them in and set them to work pursuing the profits of fish, salt, and commerce. Some even rode in carriages and cultivated connections with governors and chancellors — and still he only trusted them more.
units.literal: Cunning and unruly slaves are the bane of most people, yet Dao Jian alone took them in and set them to pursue the profits of fish, salt, and commerce. Some rode in linked carriages and cultivated connections with governors and chancellors, yet he only trusted them more.

units.zh: 終得其力，起富數千萬。
units.en: In the end, he reaped the full benefit of their efforts and built a fortune of tens of millions.
units.literal: In the end he obtained the full benefit of their efforts and built a fortune of tens of millions.

units.zh: 故曰「寧爵毋刀」，言其能使豪奴自饒而盡其力。
units.en: Hence, the saying among them: 'Better serve the Dao family than go free for noble rank' — for he could make his proud slaves prosper on their own account while still driving them to give their full measure of effort.
units.literal: Therefore, it was said: 'Would you rather go free and win noble rank than stay with the Dao family?' 'No — we will not leave the Dao' — meaning that he could make his proud slaves enrich themselves on their own while still extracting the full measure of their effort.

units.zh: 周人既纖，而師史尤甚，轉轂以百數，賈郡國，無所不至。
units.en: The people of Zhou were already shrewd and calculating, and Shi Shi was the most extreme of all. He dispatched hundreds of carts, trading across the commanderies and kingdoms, reaching every corner of the realm.
units.literal: The people of Zhou were already shrewd and calculating, and Shi Shi was the most extreme. He dispatched carts by the hundreds, trading throughout the commanderies and kingdoms, reaching every corner.

units.zh: 洛陽街居在齊秦楚趙之中，貧人學事富家，相矜以久賈，數過邑不入門，設任此等，故師史能致七千萬。
units.en: Luoyang sits at the crossroads between Qi, Qin, Chu, and Zhao. The poor there learn their trade by serving wealthy households, boasting to one another of careers spent entirely in commerce, passing through their own hometowns again and again without stopping home. With such men at his command, Shi Shi was able to amass a fortune of seventy million.
units.literal: Luoyang sits at the crossroads between Qi, Qin, Chu, and Zhao. Poor people there learn their trade by serving wealthy households, boasting to one another of long careers in commerce, passing through their own towns repeatedly without stopping at home. With such people at his disposal, Shi Shi was able to amass seventy million.

units.zh: 宣曲任氏之先，為督道倉吏。
units.en: The forebears of the Ren family of Xuanqu served as granary officials on the Dudao route.
units.literal: The ancestors of the Ren family of Xuanqu served as granary officials along the Dudao route.

units.zh: 秦之敗也，豪傑皆爭取金玉，而任氏獨窖倉粟。
units.en: When Qin collapsed, every man of power scrambled to seize gold and jade. The Ren family alone stored granary grain in underground cellars.
units.literal: When Qin collapsed, the powerful all scrambled to seize gold and jade, but the Ren family alone stored away granary grain in cellars.

units.zh: 楚漢相距滎陽也，民不得耕種，米石至萬，而豪傑金玉盡歸任氏，任氏以此起富。
units.en: When the armies of Chu and Han faced each other at Xingyang and the people could not farm, the price of grain soared to ten thousand per shi. All the gold and jade of the powerful flowed into the Ren family's hands, and they built their fortune upon it.
units.literal: When Chu and Han faced each other at Xingyang and the people could not farm, the price of grain soared to ten thousand per shi, and the gold and jade of the powerful all flowed to the Ren family. The Ren family built their fortune from this.

units.zh: 富人爭奢侈，而任氏折節為儉，力田畜。
units.en: While the other rich families competed in extravagance, the Ren family exercised restraint and lived frugally, devoting themselves to farming and animal husbandry.
units.literal: While the rich competed in extravagance, the Ren family restrained themselves and practiced frugality, devoting themselves to farming and animal husbandry.

units.zh: 田畜人爭取賤賈，任氏獨取貴善。
units.en: In farming and animal husbandry, while others competed to buy cheap, the Ren family alone chose to invest in expensive but high-quality stock.
units.literal: In farming and animal husbandry, while others competed to buy cheap, the Ren family alone chose expensive but high-quality stock.

units.zh: 富者數世。
units.en: Their wealth endured for several generations.
units.literal: They remained wealthy for several generations.

units.zh: 然任公家約，非田畜所出弗衣食，公事不畢則身不得飲酒食肉。
units.en: The Ren patriarch enforced strict family rules: they would not wear or eat anything that did not come from their own farms and herds, and until public duties were completed, no one was permitted to drink wine or eat meat.
units.literal: Yet the family rule of the Ren patriarch was strict: they would not wear or eat anything that did not come from their own farms and herds, and until public duties were completed, no one was permitted to drink wine or eat meat.

units.zh: 以此為閭里率，故富而主上重之。
units.en: By this example he led his neighborhood, and so he was both wealthy and esteemed by the sovereign himself.
units.literal: By this he set an example for his neighborhood; therefore he was both wealthy and esteemed by the sovereign.

units.zh: 塞之斥也，唯橋姚已致馬千匹，牛倍之，羊萬頭，粟以萬鐘計。
units.en: When the frontier was opened, Qiao Yao alone amassed a thousand horses, twice as many cattle, ten thousand sheep, and grain measured in the tens of thousands of zhong.
units.literal: When the frontier was opened, Qiao Yao alone amassed a thousand horses, twice as many cattle, ten thousand sheep, and grain measured in tens of thousands of zhong.

units.zh: 吳楚七國兵起時，長安中列侯封君行從軍旅，齎貸子錢，子錢家以為侯邑國在關東，關東成敗未決，莫肯與。
units.en: When the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu raised their armies in revolt, the ranked marquises and enfeoffed lords in Chang'an marched out with the army and sought loans. The moneylenders, noting that the lords' estates all lay east of the passes where the outcome of the campaign was still uncertain, refused to lend.
units.literal: When the armies of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in revolt, the ranked marquises and enfeoffed lords in Chang'an marched out with the army and sought loans at interest. The moneylenders, judging that the lords' estates lay east of the passes and the outcome of the eastern campaign was uncertain, refused to lend.

units.zh: 唯無鹽氏出捐千金貸，其息什之。
units.en: Only the Wuyan family came forward, lending a thousand in gold at tenfold interest.
units.literal: Only the Wuyan family put up a thousand in gold as a loan, at ten times interest.

units.zh: 三月，吳楚平，一歲之中，則無鹽氏之息什倍，用此富埒關中。
units.en: Within three months Wu and Chu were pacified. Within a single year, the Wuyan family's returns had multiplied tenfold, and their wealth came to rival any family within the passes.
units.literal: Within three months, Wu and Chu were pacified; within a single year, the Wuyan family's interest had multiplied tenfold. They used this to amass wealth rivaling any family within the passes.

units.zh: 關中富商大賈，大抵盡諸田，田嗇、田蘭。
units.en: The great merchants of the region within the passes were mostly surnamed Tian, led by Tian Se and Tian Lan.
units.literal: The great wealthy merchants of the region within the passes were for the most part all surnamed Tian — Tian Se and Tian Lan.

units.zh: 韋家栗氏，安陵、杜杜氏，亦巨萬。
units.en: The Li family of Wei, and the Du families of Anling and Du — these too amassed enormous fortunes.
units.literal: The Li family of Wei, the Du family of Anling and Du — these also amassed enormous fortunes.

units.zh: 此其章章尤異者也。
units.en: These are the most conspicuous and outstanding examples.
units.literal: These are the most conspicuously outstanding examples.

units.zh: 皆非有爵邑奉祿弄法犯姦而富，盡椎埋去就，與時俯仰，獲其贏利，以末致財，用本守之，以武一切，用文持之，變化有概，故足術也。
units.en: None of them grew wealthy through noble rank, fiefs, official salaries, or by twisting the law. Every one of them hammered and forged, advanced and retreated, rose and fell with the times, and seized their profits. They used commerce to build their fortunes and agriculture to preserve them, cut through obstacles with decisive action, and sustained their position through cultured management. Their adaptations followed discernible principles — their methods were truly complete.
units.literal: None of them grew rich through noble rank, landed fiefs, official salaries, or by manipulating the law and committing crimes. All of them hammered and buried, advanced and retreated, rose and fell with the times, seized their profits, used commerce to build wealth and primary occupations to preserve it, used force to cut through obstacles and culture to sustain their position. Their adaptations followed certain principles — and so their methods were complete.

units.zh: 若至力農畜，工虞商賈，為權利以成富，大者傾郡，中者傾縣，下者傾鄉里者，不可勝數。
units.en: As for those who devoted themselves to farming, herding, craftsmanship, forestry, and commerce, wielding shrewd advantage to build their wealth — dominating a commandery at the top, a county in the middle, or a village at the bottom — they are too many to count.
units.literal: As for those who devoted themselves to farming and herding, craftsmanship, forestry, and commerce, wielding influence and profit to build their wealth — those who dominated a commandery at the top, a county in the middle, and a village at the bottom — they are beyond counting.

units.zh: 夫纖嗇筋力，治生之正道也，而富者必用奇勝。
units.en: Frugality and hard labor are the orthodox path to making a living, but those who truly grow rich invariably win through unconventional methods.
units.literal: Now, frugality and physical labor are the orthodox path of managing one's livelihood, but those who truly grow rich invariably triumph through the unconventional.

units.zh: 田農，掘業，而秦揚以蓋一州。
units.en: Farming is mere digging in the earth, yet Qin Yang used it to dominate an entire province.
units.literal: Farming is mere digging, yet Qin Yang used it to dominate an entire province.

units.zh: 掘冢，姦事也，而田叔以起。
units.en: Grave-robbing is a criminal act, yet Tian Shu built his fortune upon it.
units.literal: Tomb-robbing is a criminal act, yet Tian Shu rose through it.

units.zh: 博戲，惡業也，而桓發用富。
units.en: Gambling is a disreputable trade, yet Huan Fa used it to grow wealthy.
units.literal: Gambling is a disreputable trade, yet Huan Fa grew wealthy through it.

units.zh: 行賈，丈夫賤行也，而雍樂成以饒。
units.en: Itinerant peddling is considered a lowly pursuit, yet Yong Lecheng grew prosperous through it.
units.literal: Itinerant trading is a lowly pursuit for a man, yet Yong Lecheng grew prosperous through it.

units.zh: 販脂，辱處也，而雍伯千金。
units.en: Selling grease is a humiliating occupation, yet Yong Bo amassed a thousand in gold.
units.literal: Selling fat is a humiliating occupation, yet Yong Bo amassed a thousand in gold.

units.zh: 賣漿，小業也，而張氏千萬。
units.en: Selling beverages is only a petty trade, yet the Zhang family accumulated ten million.
units.literal: Selling beverages is a petty trade, yet the Zhang family accumulated ten million.

units.zh: 灑削，薄技也，而郅氏鼎食。
units.en: Knife-grinding is a humble skill, yet the Zhi family dined from tripod vessels.
units.literal: Knife-grinding is a humble skill, yet the Zhi family ate from tripod vessels.

units.zh: 胃脯，簡微耳，濁氏連騎。
units.en: Dried tripe is a trivial, lowly trade, yet the Zhuo family rode in linked cavalcades.
units.literal: Selling dried tripe is a trivial and humble trade, yet the Zhuo family rode in linked cavalcades.

units.zh: 馬醫，淺方，張裏擊鐘。
units.en: Horse doctoring is a lowly art, yet Zhang Li struck bells at his banquets.
units.literal: Horse doctoring is a lowly art, yet Zhang Li struck bells at his feasts.

units.zh: 此皆誠壹之所致。
units.en: Every one of these fortunes was built through single-minded dedication.
units.literal: All of these were achieved through single-minded dedication.

units.zh: 由是觀之，富無經業，則貨無常主，能者輻湊，不肖者瓦解。
units.en: Seen in this light, wealth has no fixed occupation, and goods have no permanent master. The capable attract wealth like spokes converging on a hub; the incapable see it crumble away like broken tiles.
units.literal: Viewed from this perspective, wealth has no fixed occupation; goods have no permanent owner. The capable attract wealth like spokes converging on a hub, while the incapable crumble like broken tiles.

units.zh: 千金之家比一都之君，巨萬者乃與王者同樂。
units.en: A family worth a thousand in gold is the equal of a city's lord. Those who possess enormous fortunes share the same pleasures as kings.
units.literal: A family worth a thousand in gold is the equal of the lord of a city; those worth enormous sums share the same pleasures as kings.

units.zh: 豈所謂「素封」者邪？
units.en: Are these not what we call the 'Commoner Lords'?
units.literal: Are these not what are called the 'Commoner Lords'?

units.zh: 非也？
units.en: Are they not?
units.literal: Or are they not?
